findings.title: Performance model for subdivision is wrong, and the S=3 gate default rests on it
findings.description:
The "Interaction" paragraph treats per-cell occupancy as the total candidates scanned. Subdivision shrinks each cell but increases the cell count:

| Config | Cells scanned | Agents per cell | Total candidates |
|---|---|---|---|
| S=1 | 9 | ~5000 | ~45,000 |
| S=3 | 49 | ~555 | ~27,200 |

- **Subdivision alone:** the gain is about 1.65× (scan area 9r² down to 5.44r²), not the ~9× implied by "candidates loaded drops to ~5000".
- **Both together:** "candidates loaded ~555, exits after ~32" is also wrong. The `range(-S, S+1)` scan starts at corner cell (-S,-S), whose nearest point is at least ~47 units from the agent at S=3. Almost every candidate there fails the radius test, so the agent walks whole cells before accepting 32.
- **Consequence:** with a row-major scan, S=3 plus early exit can scan more candidates than S=1 plus early exit. The claim that the interventions "compose multiplicatively" is unsupported.
- **Selection bias:** "correct neighborhood is preserved" (line 56) holds for the candidate set only. At S=3, the first-k picks come from the farthest cells on one side, which A4's mean-NN-distance check may well expose.

Fix: correct the estimates. State the scan order and its effect on iterations-to-cap. Do not hard-code S=3 as the gate configuration (line 128); gate on whichever S the measurement supports. If a centre-outward cell order turns out to be needed for A3, say so in this design rather than discovering it during implementation.

findings.title: Four-way ablation in the walkthrough is not executable as designed
findings.description:
Step 3 lists four runs, but the "counter-gating" and "break enabled" pairs use identical commands. The design makes the `break` unconditional (lines 36-46), so there is no toggle. "Baseline (S=1, counter-gating)" and "Cell subdivision only (S=3, counter-gating)" cannot be produced from the slice 149 build.

This matters because the ablation is the only place the flawed model above would be caught.

Fix (lightest option): do not add a toggle. State that counter-gating numbers come from the slice 145 commit, and reduce the slice 149 runs to S=1 and S=3 with early exit. A2's baseline is then the recorded slice 145 figure or a re-run at that commit; say which.

findings.title: `S` and `cell_size` are two independent inputs with no single source of truth or production home
findings.description:
Line 53 defines `cell_size = query_radius / S`, but line 80 and the component diagram treat `cell_size` and `S` as separate configuration inputs on `BenchConfig`.

- **Silent wrong results:** nothing stops an inconsistent pair. `cell_size * S < query_radius` drops neighbors without error, which violates the project's no-silent-failure rule. The validation at lines 69-76 checks only S's range.
- **Slice 146 gap:** line 111 declares 146 "unblocked", but the setting lives only in the bench config. If the ≥100 TPS headroom is reached only at S>1, the production engine path needs to know where the value comes from. Otherwise the live server runs at S=1 and the Tier 2 NFR the gate claims to protect is not carried over.

Fix: derive `cell_size` from `query_radius` and `S` in exactly one place, or validate `cell_size * S >= query_radius` at config load. Add one sentence naming where 146 reads the value.

findings.title: Gate A5 (register spill) has no defined verification method and is not in the slice plan
findings.description:
A5 is a gate criterion, but its verification is given as "`nvcc --ptxas-info` or benchmark log" (line 124) and "`TI_PRINT_KERNEL_STATS=1` or equivalent" (line 182). Neither is a confirmed mechanism for Quadrants.

The slice plan's exit criteria for 149 are the 5× `force_total` speedup, ≥100 TPS, and 20% parity. Register spill is not among them. A gate whose check is "or equivalent" will be guessed at or skipped.

Fix: cut A5, since A2 and A3 already capture any spill cost. Alternatively, demote it to a diagnostic to run only if A2/A3 miss, and name the actual mechanism.

findings.title: Rationale for the S ≤ 8 bound is incorrect
findings.description: The text says a 17×17 scan is "larger than the physical neighborhood". The scan always covers the same physical area whatever S is, because the cells shrink as their count grows. The valid reasons for a cap are scan-cell overhead and grid cell count growing as S². Reword it, and define the bound once as a named constant rather than a literal in the validator.

findings.title: Scope matches the slice plan entry
findings.description: Both planned interventions are present. A2, A3 and A4 match the plan's exit criteria exactly. The default S=1 keeps backward compatibility as the plan requires. Out-of-scope items (distance-ranked k-nearest, GPU prefix sum, world-server wiring) match the plan. The document is proportionate for an Effort 2/5 slice.

findings.title: Break placement deviates from the plan wording with sound justification
findings.description: The plan says to replace counter-gating "in `get_neighbors_first_k`". The design explains that the seam function cannot issue a `break` and places it in the caller's innermost loop instead. This keeps the A7 swap point intact. The `max_neighbors > 0` guard preserves the uncapped path. Early exit selects the same first-k set as counter-gating, so it is behavior-preserving at S=1.

findings.title: Tier 2 NFR restated with a specific target
findings.description: The 60 TPS at N=50k target is restated, and the 100 TPS gate is explained as headroom over it.

findings.title: Dependencies and boundaries are correct
findings.description: The slice depends only on 145, matching the plan. `TickResult`, the world-server contract, and the numpy/numba backends are untouched. No new I/O paths or message types are introduced, so failure-mode enumeration does not apply beyond the config validation, which fails explicitly.
